## Which clients the rate points toward, and what is proven
1. WHOAMI8.74961/s total: managed status lines are the strongest recurring source candidate, not uniquely identified. At this deployed source, Copilot statusline_copilot issues one whoami per render (crates/cli/src/main.rs:2571-2582); its managed refresh is10s plus host render events (crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs:175-205). Claude's script runs whoami--pane on every render (harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh:84-96), with host-controlled render rate. CLI acting-seat resolution/explicit whoami/commit trailers share this endpoint. For scale only,7.75successful/s equals about77.5 default10s timer equivalents before event-driven renders; this is NOT a measured seat count.

   Refusals were exactly90 in each90s subwindow: a very regular~1Hz failed-identity workload. This is the best lead for the previously sampled Claude census, but not a proven census count. identity.rs:1453-1459 calls stray_pane only when a request has a pane with no running owner; no-caller, asserted-ID-only, contradictory and other refusals may skip it. The census scans every Claude record before pane filtering (double_seat.rs:125-159; harnesses/proc.rs:456-474). Census frames were actually observed in F222 samples2d3d51cd; route counts now show sustained refusal demand, but no refusal-code/pane/client dimension to assign it to a particular status line. Refused WHOAMI rate alone must not be relabeled 'one census/s'.

2. Heartbeat3.62762/s: receiver/claim lease renewals, not roster polling. Native Copilot posts /v1/inbox/heartbeat immediately then on server renew_after_ms (.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:1462-1497); default60s lease renews after20s (delivery/mod.rs:356-369,436-459), consistent in scale with~73 continuously renewed native receivers. OMP body-claim renewals can also share this endpoint; no exact client/seat count can be derived. This route does not use WHOAMI or the Claude census.

3. Seats1.33883/s,100%scope=local: source points to local-authority roster consumers. Federation fan-in is the only identified steady configured1Hz source per healthy peer (federation/fanin.rs:199-247; config.rs:214); native Copilot registration/retry uses the identical scope=local query (extension.mjs:218-245), as do commit-trailer hooks and peers check (cli/client.rs:383-386,commit_trailers.rs:19-35,peers.rs:99-123). Therefore 'all federation' or 'one specific peer' is not proven. Zero registration-attempt growth weakens an active native-re-registration explanation, without identifying all remaining producers.

   What IS eliminated for these GET requests: OMP's ordinary boot/reattach/child-wait caller uses bare /v1/seats (.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/daemon-http.ts:214-215; rust-runtime.ts:326-339,765-805,992-1001), whose delta is zero. Human/native list uses sizes=true (cli/client.rs:360-378), also zero; status lines use WHOAMI rather than seats. Thus 'OMP periodically refreshes the full roster' does not explain the measured241 reads.

   Tie to actual sampled hot path: GET seats calls SqliteStatus::read(None), processes all durable rows/status correlations, then filters (http/mod.rs seats handler; store/status.rs:16-36,107-145). At the observed rate this is1.33883 full status projections/s, scaling with all durable rows/assignments—not just the returned live seats. F222's samples directly showed this route/status path plus asynchronous SQLite worker work. We still cannot assign all SQLite-worker CPU to this route from independent route counters; CPU-per-request/SQL correlation was not measured.

Claude hooks can reach the same census through activity/fyi::bound_seat when seatless/unowned (http/fyi.rs:424-436), but these routes grew only7 and2 respectively, with no refusals. They are much less frequent demand than WHOAMI in this interval; counter rates do not show whether any particular request scanned records.
